generation: Speedmax CFR / CF SLX Disc, gen 5 (2021–2025)
identify: Disc brakes, a bolt-on Canyon base bar (flat CP0019 or rise CP0021) on a stack of spacers, and a carbon 'spring' plate that carries the arm pads. A storage lid on the top tube and a bladder in the down tube. Frame code R085 (CFR) or R091 (CF SLX) on Canyon's papers. The 2026 bike (gen 6) has a closed one-piece cockpit on a post instead.

cockpit.steerer: 1-1/8 in steerer with Canyon wedge expander (Canyon part EP1296-01 'Wedge extension 1 1/8'); the stem/cockpit clamp is Canyon-only
cockpit.stem: Canyon proprietary cockpit clamp in a short or a long version (exploded drawing lists CP0019 basebar short/flat and long/flat with separate stem covers S and L). Canyon's spec for a size M CFR lists the long flatbar with an 85 mm stem.
cockpit.stack_system: A base spacer in four positions (High, Medium as delivered, Low, Slammed) plus thin spacers up to 40 mm. An extra angled spacer between the spring plate and the extension adds 15 mm. Canyon gives 110 mm of pad-height range per size.
cockpit.reach_system: The pads have three positions front to back and two side to side. The extensions are telescopic and slide after loosening two bolts. The cockpit comes short or long; the long one adds about 20 mm of pad reach. Canyon gives about 54 mm of pad-reach range per size.
cockpit.angle_system: An angled spacer of about 3° or 6° comes with the bike, on up to 25 mm of spacers; a second one can sit between the spring plate and the extension. Canyon's Angle Fitting Kit goes to 22.5°.
cockpit.notes: Pad width is the most-cited limit: a Canyon-endorsed fitter gave stock pad widths of 88 / 140 / 159 mm (Dec 2020) and later called the maximum about 175 mm centre to centre; Canyon told an owner no wider spring exists. Canyon refused to give an owner the arm-pad bolt pattern, so third-party pad fit is trial and error. In July 2026 Canyon e-mailed Speedmax owners that untested third-party reach extenders/adapters are not approved and may void the warranty (owners' posts). Fitter: the gen-5 bike is shorter and taller than the rim SLX before it.

stock_range.note: Canyon armpad stack/reach (m/n) for the gen-5 CFR Di2; measuring point not stated. A Canyon-endorsed fitter read the reach range as the short cockpit and added ~20 mm for the long one.
Fitter: S reaches 460 only with the long cockpit.
Fitter: M reaches about 483 with the long cockpit.
Fitter: L maxes out at 504 with long cockpit and pads fully forward.
Fitter: XL reaches about 528 with the long cockpit.

effect.text: Adds 25 mm of reach and sets extension angle from 5° to 22.5° in 3.5° steps (the top 5° comes from the carbon spring).

evidence.says: Canyon lists it for Speedmax CFR and SLX (R085, R91): +25 mm reach, 5–22.5° in 3.5° steps; out of stock in the US store.
The gen-5 CFR Di2 page offers the aftermarket angle fitting kit as an extra (+25 mm reach, up to 22.5°).

parts.needs: Uses the bike's carbon spring for the last 5°; fixing screws included. Members-only/out of stock in several regions.

parts.model: Long cockpit (CP0019 Triathlon Flatbar long + long stem cover)

effect.text: Swapping the short cockpit for the long one moves pads and base bar about 20 mm forward.

evidence.says: Canyon's R085 (CFR) and R091 (CF SLX) exploded drawings list a short and a long CP0019 flat basebar with matching stem covers.
Canyon-endorsed fitter: the online Pad X ranges are for the short cockpit; the long one adds about 20 mm (S 460, M 483, L 504, XL 528), and in the US it had to be ordered separately.
Same fitter (2022): on a small you would need the long cockpit, an aftermarket order in the US.

parts.needs: Cockpit swap with brake/shift routing through the front end; order via Canyon service (not listed in the web shop).

effect.text: Longer telescopic extension and grips for riders with long forearms; moves the hands, not the pads.

evidence.says: Owner: ask Canyon for the 'GP0243 Aerobar Large'; not on the web shop; both the telescopic part and grips are longer.
Fitter prescribes a size L CFR with short stem, mid spacer, tilt wedge and probably the long aero extension for a 193 cm rider.
XL owner with 39–40 cm forearms chose the long extensions.

parts.needs: Owners report Canyon tends to sell the whole cockpit rather than the extension alone.

effect.text: Single mono-grip extension with front shift button; 112 mm upswept grip, 36° upsweep, 40 mm mounting area. Changes hand position, not pad position.

evidence.says: Canyon: fits Speedmax SLX (R091) and CFR (R085); not compatible with frame size XL; Shimano or SRAM version; on sale at EUR 82.99 (was 237.99).

parts.needs: Pick the Shimano or SRAM shifter version. Sizes XS–L only.

effect.text: Same part as above, on an XL frame.

parts.reason_incompatible: Canyon states the Monogrip is not compatible with bikes in frame size XL.

evidence.says: Product page warns the Monogrip does not fit frame size XL.

parts.model: Winkel-Spacer (angle spacer) for Speedmax SLX/CFR, RI10125

effect.text: One-piece 10°, 15° or 20° angle spacer that also moves the bars about 20 mm forward; stock height spacers still usable.

evidence.says: Maker lists it for disc-brake Speedmax SLX/CFR: 10/15/20°, ~20 mm more reach, works with Canyon spacers; with the 20 mm base spacer add at least 30 mm of 5 mm spacers.
Canyon-endorsed fitter: the Rad Sport tilt/extender works only on the disc SLX, not the rim SLX.
Owner runs the highest-angle Radsport angle spacer on his disc Speedmax.
Owner of a 2024 Speedmax has a Radsport Ibert adapter/extender fitted.

parts.needs: Bolts 22/35/40 mm included; stacking a stock 3.5°/7° wedge on top needs longer riser bolts (maker's table). Canyon's July 2026 e-mail says untested third-party extenders may void the warranty.

effect.text: Full-carbon long armrest shells that bolt to the Canyon computer mount; the maker gives no reach or width figures.

evidence.says: Maker: for disc-brake Speedmax SLX and CFR (mono cockpit only); mounts via an included aluminium bracket to the Canyon computer mount (not included).

parts.model: Ascalon adapter, Canyon Speedmax CFR / CF SLX (monopost), tilt adjustable

effect.text: Mounts AeroCoach Ascalon extensions on the Speedmax monopost at 15° or 25°, fine-tuned with the bike's 3° wedges. Reach depends on the Ascalon length chosen (255–305 mm).

evidence.says: Adapter dropdown lists 'Canyon Speedmax CFR / CF SLX (monopost) - tilt adjustable' in 15° or 25°, compatible with the bike's 3° wedges; adapters only work with Ascalon extensions.

parts.needs: AeroCoach Ascalon extensions (sold separately); warranty only with Ascalon extensions.

effect.text: Plate that carries TriRig-style super-extensions/cups on the CFR front end; TriRig publishes no reach/stack figures for the Canyon version.

evidence.says: Search listing of TriRig's product page names Canyon Speedmax CFR among compatible bikes (CF SLX not named); USD 195 shown.
TriRig, 16 Feb 2026 (before gen 6 launched): Super-X plates now available for the Canyon Speedmax.

parts.needs: Extensions/cups sold separately. CF SLX shares the same cockpit parts in Canyon's drawings, but TriRig names only the CFR: confirm with TriRig.

parts.model: Metron TFE EVO extensions adapter for Canyon Speedmax CFR, V3166

effect.text: Bike-specific carbon adapter (107 g) to mount Vision Metron TFE EVO extensions on the Speedmax CFR.

evidence.says: Search listing: 'Vision Metron TFE EVO Extensions Adapter for Canyon Speedmax CFR - V3166', carbon, 107 g, EUR 112.60 (page itself returned 403).
Search listing gives the Speedmax CFR adapter code 670-0546000970 among the TFE EVO adapters.

parts.needs: Vision Metron TFE EVO extensions (USD 740 at Vision US). The fit on this generation comes from the retailer's listing; confirm with Vision.

parts.model: Carbon mono-bar extension for Canyon Speedmax

effect.text: Longer carbon replacement for Canyon's aluminium mono-bar extension; moves the hands further forward. Length not published.

evidence.says: Owner (Speedmax CF SLX 8 thread): Stride's carbon mono-bar is longer than Canyon's and better made; shipped from Poland in about a month.
Same owner (Sep 2026): the longest Canyon mono-bar was not long enough, so he bought Stride's extra-long one.

parts.needs: Not tested by Canyon. The maker's website was unavailable when we checked.

effect.text: Plates that move the arm cups outward to widen the narrow stock pad width (~175 mm c-c max).

evidence.says: Owner fitted Wingspan Extenders plus TriRig open-back carbon arm cups on a Speedmax CF SLX; more comfortable with the wider fit (Feb 2023).
Owner added Wingspan XL Extenders on a 2024 Speedmax CF/SLX 8; so far so good (Mar 2025).
Conflicting: another owner says TriRig told him the extenders are not compatible with the Speedmax.
TriRig needed the bolt pattern to confirm fit; Canyon refused to supply it, citing warranty.

parts.needs: TriRig or other arm cups with a matching bolt pattern; check with TriRig first (mixed answers).

parts.model: Scoops arm cups (on the stock carbon spring)

effect.text: Replacement arm cups; one owner found they add at most ~1 cm of width and their pre-drilled holes hard to line up with the Canyon plate.

evidence.says: Owner fitted TriRig closed-back Scoops; pre-drilled holes were hard to match to the bike's hole layout; little width gained.
Another owner fitted TriRig full open-back carbon arm cups (with Wingspan Extenders) on a Speedmax CF SLX.

parts.needs: Undrilled version means drilling carbon; check hole alignment before buying.

parts.model: Speedmax CF SLX 60 mm Spacer Kit (GP0017-01) / 9° Spacer Kit (GP0018-01)

effect.text: Rim-brake SLX riser and angle kits.

parts.reason_incompatible: Canyon lists both kits only for the rim-brake Speedmax CF SLX (R40) dual-tower cockpit, model year 2018 and older; the disc bike uses a different spacer column.

evidence.says: 60 mm kit: Speedmax CF SLX (R40), dual-tower, MY2018 and older.
9° kit: Speedmax CF SLX (R40), dual-tower, MY2018 and older.

parts.model: AeroShield / cockpit post of the 2026 Speedmax (gen 6)

effect.text: The new closed cockpit and its head-tube post.

parts.reason_incompatible: Canyon France told an owner there is no front-end compatibility between the previous and the new Speedmax generation; the gen-6 cockpit post slides into a different head tube.

evidence.says: Owner reports Canyon France by phone: no front-end compatibility between old and new generation Speedmax.
Gen 6 replaces the bolt-on aerobar with a closed AeroShield on a post that clamps inside the head tube.

gaps: Pad reference point of Canyon's armpad stack/reach table not stated; fitter reads the reach range as the short cockpit (long cockpit +~20 mm). CF SLX assumed to share the CFR table (same cockpit parts in Canyon's R085/R091 drawings) but the CF SLX page was not checked.
Arm-pad bolt spacing and extension clamp diameter not published; Canyon refused to give the bolt pattern to an owner.
Canyon 'Pro Spacer' (+25 / +30 mm reach) described by the Canyon-endorsed fitter in Oct 2022 as not yet public; whether it became the Angle Fitting Kit (+25 mm) is not confirmed.
Stock angled wedge angle reported as 3°/6° (Canyon cockpit guide) vs 3.5°/7° (Radsport Ibert); Angle Fitting Kit uses 3.5° steps.
Pad width: fitter gave 88/140/159 mm (2020) and later ~175 mm c-c maximum; measuring basis differs or changed.

TriRig product page and Vision product page blocked (429/403); compatibility taken from search listings and blog. AeroCoach Speedmax adapter price unclear (dropdown shows an add-on of GBP 285 over a GBP 115 base); price left null.
No owner report found for 51 Speedshop, Wattshop or Profile Design extensions on the gen-5 cockpit; Radsport Ibert stock-bolt combinations and Canyon's warranty position on them are owner hearsay.
Canyon rise bar (CP0021) base-bar height change not quantified; long cockpit not sold in Canyon's web shop (price unknown).
